title: Key transit routes
steps: Tokyo → Yamagata: Yamagata Shinkansen "Tsubasa" direct from Tokyo Station, ≈2h22m fastest (up to ≈2h45m), roughly hourly. Every seat is reserved — book all 8 together. ⚠ ≈¥11,450 one-way in an ordinary reserved car (¥6,050 base fare + ¥5,400 express charge) — confirm at booking.

Yamagata → Yamadera: JR Senzan Line direct, ≈19-23 min, roughly hourly. ⚠ ≈¥260 cash / ≈¥253 IC one-way, corroborated via aggregator only — confirm at the station. Yamadera Station is a ≈10 min walk from Risshaku-ji's base entrance.

Yamagata → Oishida (for Ginzan Onsen): JR Ōu Line — local train ≈50 min, or Tsubasa ≈28 min (extra limited-express surcharge). Suica/IC cards are not usable at Ōishida Station per multiple Japanese sources (not confirmed against JR East directly) — buy a paper ticket.

Oishida → Ginzan Onsen (the anchor transfer, carried with luggage): Hanagasa Bus, Ginzan Line, ≈35-40 min, ¥1,000/adult one-way, cash only (half fare, ¥500, for children and disabled passengers), no reservation needed. The operator runs a different timetable per season, each on its own page — the Apr 1 – Oct 24, 2026 table is the one covering this trip, and it carries more daily departures than the Dec 1 – Mar 31 winter table. First bus leaves Oishida ≈6:40. ⚠ Don't plan a late arrival around 18:21 — that is the last bus out of Ginzan Onsen (the operator's note reads 「最終便18:21発」), not the last one in; the final inbound run is earlier, and the seasonal table is hard to read across its columns, so confirm the day's last Oishida departure before committing to a slow morning in the city. ⚠ The operator's summary page still advertises 5 round trips a day while its seasonal timetable lists more — read the timetable itself, and confirm the day of. Missing a bus can mean waiting over two hours, and the longest gap falls around midday. Board early with the group's luggage; if the bus can't take it all, a taxi (≈20 min, ≈¥6,500-8,000/car, 2-3 cars for 8 people — call Ōbanazawa Taxi 0237-23-2525 ahead) is the fallback.

Ginzan Onsen → Oishida (return): two departures to avoid, both flagged in the operator's own service notes — the 14:55 does not connect to a Tokyo-bound Yamagata Shinkansen (the operator's 上り — the up-line runs toward Tokyo, which is the direction this group leaves in, and geographically south), and the last bus, 18:21, is expected to be crowded with no extra service added. The operator points passengers at 16:35 instead; 13:25 is the earlier clean option. With eight people, luggage and two low-mobility travelers, pick one of those two and confirm it at Ginzanso the night before.
Getting around Yamagata city: the station area is walkable (most central hotels are 5-8 min on foot), with a taxi rank and bus terminal directly outside the station.
